purpose: Every SVG under website/public/diagrams/** (42 files), with the page/doc that embeds it, the concept it depicts, the ADR it maps to, the FORBIDDEN legacy terms that appear as visible text, and the reconstruction treatment. Grounded by reading each SVG's title/desc/text and grepping consumers across website/**, docs/** and website/content/**.

consumer_legend.REF-PT: docs/reference/pt/completa.md (documentation mirror, not a rendered website page)

svgs.concept: BanzAI cognitive engine — a question becomes a grounded answer across evidence/cognitive/model planes; model drafts, BanzAI verifies.
svgs.rationale: The three 'planes' are BanzAI's internal cognition, not the ecosystem layer stack; BanzAI not drawn as a layer. Not embedded on a rendered PT surface.

svgs.concept: Protocol boundary — humans/operators reach BANZA via BanzAI; operators, bank/EMIS infra and regulators sit outside; no funds flow through BANZA.
svgs.rationale: Clean boundary framing. Review only that BanzAI is shown as interface (correct), not a layer, when ch.4/12 are rewritten.

svgs.concept: Conformance pipeline — operator implementation -> sandbox endpoint -> banza-conformance -> evidence report; auto-publish/federation gated on M2/M3.
svgs.rationale: No L-levels visible. Align labels to the L2 certification model (Profile->CertifiedImplementation->CertificationRecord) when ch.7 is rewritten.

svgs.concept: Conformance flow (5 steps + evaluation) — 'a conformidade e medida, nao concedida'; ends in Open Trust Evaluation.
shows_forbidden: 'demonstrar um ambito de conformidade (L0 a L4)' — L0-L4 presented as a certification range
svgs.rationale: Demote L0-L4 from a headline certification range to conformance scope; reframe to the ADR-064/066 certification model.

svgs.concept: Controlled federation — technical interop != federated production; Open Trust Evaluation gates between Operator A/B; fail-closed.
shows_forbidden: 'Ambito L3+ compativel' — certification level L3+ shown as a gate criterion
svgs.rationale: Reword 'L3+' from a certification level to the conformance scope required for federation, per the L0-L4 clarification (scope, not public tier).

svgs.concept: Decision -> mitigated-risk matrix — protocol design rationale (contracts-first, PASS!=certificate, protocol/operator separation, offline root, signed BRL, BanzAI non-normative).
svgs.rationale: 'PASS != certificado' is a correct disclaimer. No forbidden framing.

svgs.concept: Developer flow — sandbox & conformance, no real money; 7 numbered steps (Ler referencia -> Implementar -> Proteger -> Conformidade -> Evidencia -> Corrigir -> Publicar metadata assinada).
svgs.rationale: A 7-step DEVELOPER flow, NOT the retired 7-step operator journey (the operator/validation journey correctly has 9 steps). Legitimate, but review that it is not confused with the journey during the ch.13 rewrite.

svgs.concept: Two planes — conformance evidence (measured, self-published) vs legal authorisation (from regulator, outside BANZA).
svgs.rationale: Filename says 'certificate' but visible text uses 'Autorizacao legal'; no 'certificado de operador'. Correct cert!=authorisation framing.

svgs.concept: Inter-operator federated payment — initiator/sender/receiver across Operator A/B with shared trace_id; peers evaluate signed metadata.
shows_forbidden: 'Nenhum acordo bilateral necessario.' — absolute 'sem acordos bilaterais' claim (split across two text lines)
svgs.rationale: Qualify to 'sem acordos bilaterais previos entre cada par' (matching the reference body), never the absolute claim.

svgs.concept: Governance process — RFC -> discussion -> acceptance -> ADR -> implementation -> official protocol; open to all operators.
svgs.rationale: Clean governance flow.

svgs.concept: Double-entry posting — debit consumer wallet balanced by credits to merchant + fees; sums to zero.
svgs.rationale: Financial-invariant illustration; unaffected by M2.19G.

svgs.concept: Local execution model — each operator runs the protocol locally; BANZA is rules, not a central server (HTTP analogy).
svgs.rationale: Correct 'protocol not server' framing.

svgs.concept: Normative hierarchy N1-N5 (Principles -> Invariants -> ADRs -> RFCs -> Implementation guides); each level binds those below.
svgs.rationale: N1-N5 are NORMATIVE levels (uses 'NIVEL'), not the ecosystem 'camadas' stack and not certification levels. Not the forbidden 4/5-layer architecture.

svgs.concept: Operator conformance lifecycle (6 steps) — candidate -> sandbox -> PASS -> publish signed metadata -> registry index -> peer Open Trust Evaluation; fail-closed.
svgs.rationale: No L-levels; 'nao e certificado' disclaimer present. Align 'PASS' wording to the certification model on the ch.7 rewrite.

svgs.concept: L0 sandbox operator endpoints — GET /health and /.well-known/banza/operator.json minimal manifest with sandbox safety properties.
shows_forbidden: 'Endpoints L0 do operador de sandbox' (title) + 'certification_level' manifest field — L0 as a certification level
svgs.rationale: Reframe L0 as sandbox conformance scope, not a certification level; keep the endpoints content.

svgs.concept: Operator conformance-LEVELS chart — L0 Sandbox, L1 Payment, L2 Initiation, L3 Inter-Op, L4 External; cumulative.
shows_forbidden: L0
L1
L2
L3
L4 — the certification-levels-as-levels chart ('Niveis de Conformidade de Operadores', 'Cada nivel e cumulativo')
svgs.rationale: This IS the retired L0-L4 certification-levels diagram. Replace with the L2 certification model (Certification Profile -> CertifiedImplementation -> CertificationRecord + states), demoting L0-L4 to conformance scope.

svgs.concept: Architecture overview — 'O OPERADOR EXECUTA / O BANZA DEFINE / FORA DO PROTOCOLO'; BanzAI as primary interface at the boundary; no fund flow.
svgs.rationale: Not forbidden as-is (BanzAI = interface, no layer count), but this is the primary architecture diagram and does NOT depict the canonical THREE-LAYER model (L1 protocol / L2 certification / L3 scheme). Rewrite to the three-layer architecture.

svgs.concept: Protocol architecture — BanzAI guides -> engines verify -> evidence proves -> governance decides; machine-to-machine rail bypasses BanzAI.
svgs.rationale: BanzAI shown as flow entry, not a layer (good). Rewrite/augment to also carry the three-layer model and the 'Rust decides / Qwen explains' authority rule explicitly.

svgs.concept: Reference-operator internal architecture — CAMADA 1 (orchestration) + CAMADA 2 (financial core) + published protocol artifacts.
shows_forbidden: 'L0 health check · L1 carteiras e QR · L2 liquidacao · L3 federacao · L4 acquiring' footer — L0-L4 certification levels
svgs.rationale: Remove the L0-L4 footer level framing (the two 'CAMADA 1/2' are internal operator layers, not the ecosystem stack — those are fine). Consider whether a generic 'reference operator' internal diagram belongs on a protocol surface at all vs Operador Zero.

svgs.concept: Roadmap M1-M6 — Spec (done) -> Production Trust -> First Operator -> BanzAI Operational -> Validation Studio (M5) -> Public Launch.
shows_forbidden: 'Estudio de Validacao' (M5) — legacy validation-tooling framing adjacent to 'Validation Workbench'
svgs.rationale: Reword the M5 label away from a 'Validation Studio/Workbench' product; also verify the roadmap milestones still match the three-layer/M2.19 reality.

svgs.concept: Trust infrastructure — 5 PKI levels (Root Key offline -> Key Manifest -> Issuing Keys -> signed metadata/BRL/evidence -> operator network); offline verification.
shows_forbidden: 'cinco camadas' present ONLY in the non-rendered <desc> accessibility text (visible text uses 'NIVEL 1-5')
svgs.rationale: Reword the <desc> to avoid 'cinco camadas' (which reads as the forbidden 5-layer architecture); the visible PKI-level hierarchy is legitimate.

svgs.concept: BanzAI as protocol agent — guides operator from manifest to federation; agent not authority; rule provenance RFC/ADR -> release.
svgs.rationale: BanzAI drawn as an 'Agent' node, not a layer. Referenced by decisions.ts/home test — review that its provenance/agent framing matches ADR-067 'single interface' and does not imply BanzAI-as-layer (ADR-041 is retired framing).

svgs.concept: BanzAI-guided operator journey — 9 steps (Ler Referencia -> Manifest -> SimB -> Conformidade -> Trust -> Evidence Bundle -> Publicar metadata -> Verificacao por pares -> Federacao).
svgs.rationale: Correct 9-step count, but the step NAMES differ from the canonical journey (Discovery, Manifest, Keys, Conformance, Interoperability, Trust, Federation, Evidence Bundle, Certification Readiness). Align labels to ADR-067's nine canonical steps.

svgs.concept: 'Who does what' — regulators / operator / Rust engines / BanzAI / peers / open governance, each with role + boundary.
svgs.rationale: Authority-boundary diagram (candidate canonical). Review it reflects the three-layer owners and cert!=admission!=authorisation.

svgs.concept: Rule provenance — RFC/ADR -> specs/contracts -> BANZA reference -> engines verify -> BanzAI guides -> operator executes; AI output is not a rule.
svgs.rationale: Correct 'Rust decides / AI is not a rule' framing.

svgs.concept: Single-answer pipeline — one Rust router, exact terminals (0 Qwen calls), one Qwen synthesis, Rust factual validator before publishing.
svgs.rationale: BanzAI ask-mode internals; unaffected.

svgs.concept: Open Trust Evaluation — 5 evidence inputs, 10 deterministic checks, Routing-Allowed vs Fail-Closed; Operator A/B, no central arbiter.
svgs.rationale: Canonical trust diagram; registry not framed as certified-operator list; disclaimers present.
